messages:
incident-bot: PAGING ALERT — runtime-decode (streaming-prod, us-west-2) p95/p99 spike detected. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~650ms, p99 from ~1.8s to ~6.2s. Elevated 5xx for streaming endpoints. Triggered at 12:02 UTC. @maya please ack

maya: acked. saw the alert, joining. any immediate customer page?

leo: getting customer reports of stalls in long-lived streams, several sessions hung for >10s. frontdoor 502s increasing. I can see a tail distribution skew.

ashley: I'm seeing kernel level errors on a subset of hosts: repeated pagefault churn in dmesg on gpu nodes. posting sample:```[ 12345.678901] nvhost: pagefault at 0x7ff… trace … compilepath: evicting KV cache```

zane: interesting — we rolled a small kernel/compilepath change last night to pick up TRT8 flash-attn optimizations. Could be related. Rollout window was 02:30–03:00 UTC.

maya: ok timeline matches. can we confirm which hosts are impacted?

leo: filtering by image tag shows nodes with kernel v5.14.23-cp1 have the spike. older ones v5.14.22 stable.

devops-bot: @channel nodes-in-group gpu-pool-a: 12/48 report high pagefaults; kernel version 5.14.23-cp1; recent deploy id: deploy-2026-03-14-kernel-optimizations.

ashley: logs show KV cache evictions correlate with long decode tails. When eviction happens, per-token latency jumps. suspect compilepath change interacting with FlashAttention memory layout.

ops-lead: priority = P1. Customer impact: several mid-market customers in US seeing degraded streaming quality. Escalating to on-call SRE and runtime infra.

maya: immediate mitigation options? rollback kernel on affected pool, or route live traffic to Dedicated fallback pool?

zane: rollback of kernel is heavier and will require node cycling, but should be doable as an emergency. We have a live routing policy that can failover to fallback model variant (cpu-safe) but that increases token cost and latency.

leo: temporary per-node cordon + drain could pull pods off bad nodes and shift to healthy ones. Might avoid full rollback if capacity exists.

maya: do we have spare capacity in other pools to handle streaming load?

devops-bot: capacity report: other gpu pools at 75% avg; can absorb up to ~30% additional load for short bursts. autoscaler configured but scaling spin-up for reserved hosts is ~8–12min.

ashley: also note that streaming requests with long KV caches will hit the issue more, so simply moving short sessions won't fully mitigate. Prefer to isolate kernel-rolled nodes.

ops-lead: immediate plan: 1) cordon impacted nodes, 2) drain low-priority pods first, 3) reroute new streaming connections to healthy pools, 4) prepare kernel rollback image if cordon/drain insufficient.

maya: assigning takers. @leo you handle cordon/drain and routing rules. @zane you prepare rollback artifacts and test on a canary node. @ashley monitor memory/KV eviction metrics and confirm correlation. I'll coordinate customer comms and handoff.

leo: starting cordon on gpu-pool-a nodes with high pagefaults. running: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12 && kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ashley: adding an alert: `metrics.alerts.streaming.kernel_eviction_rate` bumped to SEV2. posting dashboard snippet: p95 token latency (by node) https://redwood.internal/dash/streaming/p95-by-node — you can see a handful of nodes ~3x higher.

zane: spun up a canary node with kernel v5.14.22 rollback and ran the internal stress harness for streaming decode with flash-attn enabled. Canary shows no pagefault churn and stable p99 ~1.9s.

devops-bot: canary test OK on node-canary-3; cpu/gpu temps normal; no compilepath errors in dmesg for 30m.

maya: good. @zane proceed with rollback plan but coordinate maintenance window with SRE. We'll avoid full cluster restart if possible.

ops-lead: customer impact note: support already opened tickets for 3 customers — product team advised to send proactive update about degraded streaming for US region and mitigation in progress. @maya can you draft a short status?

maya: drafting: "We detected increased streaming latency in US-west-2 due to a kernel/compilepath regression introduced in a recent runtime optimization rollout. Our team is isolating affected hosts and preparing a rollback; streaming traffic will be shifted to healthy pools while we remediate. We’ll provide an update within 30 minutes."

leo: cordon/drain complete for 8 nodes so far. New session routing showing 15% shift to other pools, errors down ~20% from peak. Still seeing tail spikes on remaining impacted nodes.

ashley: confirmed KV eviction rate follows node status. when node is drained, sessions removed, per-node p99 drops back to baseline. inference: issue is localized to kernel variant.

zane: rolling rollback to remaining affected nodes now using image rollback job: `./ops/rollbacks/rollback-kernel --group gpu-pool-a --to 5.14.22` will take ~6–9min per node. doing 4 at a time.

devops-bot: rollback job started. progress: 4/40 nodes rolled back.

sre-oncall: note — monitor end-to-end client reconnect behavior. Some clients may retry aggressively and cause short-term surge in new connections. Apply connection backoff if necessary.

leo: applying short-term connection-limit policy via frontdoor rate-limiter to reduce retry storm. Patch applied.

maya: status update for customers: "We are actively rolling back a kernel variant that is impacting streaming performance in us-west-2. Traffic is being shifted to healthy capacity. Error rates and latencies are improving; we expect to restore normal service within 45–60 minutes." posting now.

ops-lead: good. keep cadence updates every 15 mins. prepare postmortem runbook: collect deploy id, kernel git sha, host list, dmesg snippets, and the exact compilepath flags that landed.

ashley: capturing logs: attaching snippets to incident ticket INC-2026-3287. Key lines: `compilepath: set flag --enable-flashattn-opt=1` and `trt: registered kernel variant id 0x9a` + eviction traces.

zane: follow-up: branch `runtime/compilepath/flashattn-opt` had a small change to allocator behavior for KV cache alignment. that likely changed eviction thresholds on certain GPU drivers.

leo: rollbacks continuing. p99 trending down on overall cluster from 6.2s -> 2.1s after first 12 nodes rolled back.

maya: I'm going to prepare handoff summary for next on-call in 30 minutes. Handoff will include affected node list, rollback progress, and customer comms.

ops-lead: we should also plan a controlled repro in staging with the exact kernel+compilepath combo and heavy streaming to validate before we consider re-landing the optimization.

zane: agreed. we'll block the PR until full repro and fix. likely either tweak allocator alignment or add a guard for evictions when KV usage crosses a threshold.

devops-bot: rollback complete on group gpu-pool-a: 40/40 nodes rolled back. final cluster p95/p99 back to baseline within 18 minutes of final rollback.

maya: great. final customer update I sent: "Issue mitigated by rolling back a kernel optimization introduced in last night's rollout. We are conducting a full investigation and will follow up with a postmortem containing root cause and remediation items. If you continue to see issues, please ping support."

ashley: collecting postmortem artifacts now. tagging relevant PRs and compilepath commits.

ops-lead: next steps: 1) reproduce in staging, 2) add unit/regression test for KV eviction scenario, 3) add metric guard to detect early eviction anomalies and auto-rollback policy, 4) schedule postmortem with runtime, infra, and QA.

maya: handing off to next on-call @sre-oncall for monitoring window and follow-up. summary attached to ticket INC-2026-3287.

sre-oncall: ack. will monitor for 2h and keep channel updated. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — root cause suspected: compilepath allocator change + kernel variant interaction causing KV cache evictions leading to streaming decode tail latency. Postmortem assigned: PM-runtime; SEV: P1 -> downgraded after rollback.

maya: closing thread once postmortem doc is created. good job everyone."
